title: Lock Opportunity Amount after Closed Won

requirement.summary: Add a single ValidationRule on Opportunity that blocks any save reducing Amount once StageName is Closed Won, using PRIORVALUE(Amount) guarded against insert, with a named bypass for exempt users/integrations and an error message that states the problem and the fix; scoped to one metadata artefact with no new object, field, or automation.

clarifications.question: Does the Sales team enter Amount directly on the Opportunity, or is Amount rolling up from Opportunity Products / Line Items?
clarifications.why: Validation rules don't fire on an Opportunity when an Opportunity Line Item write is what changed the total, so a rule guarding Amount never runs in a line-item-driven process (admin/validation-rules, Questions to Ask row 1).
clarifications.answer_shape: Given [Products are / are not enabled on Opportunity], When a user edits [Amount directly / a Line Item quantity or price], Then the validation rule [fires on the Opportunity save / must instead be a record-triggered flow on OpportunityLineItem].
clarifications.answer: Amount is typed directly on the Opportunity by the rep. We do not use Opportunity Products / line items, so nothing rolls up into Amount.

clarifications.question: Does any Workflow Rule field update, Process Builder, or other automation write to Opportunity Amount after the record saves?
clarifications.why: Validation rules are not re-run after a workflow field update re-saves the record, so an existing post-save writer would make the new rule silently not a database invariant (admin/validation-rules, Questions to Ask row 2).
clarifications.answer_shape: Given the current org automation on Opportunity, When Amount changes after Closed Won, Then either no other automation writes Amount post-save, or the named automation is listed and migrated to a before-save flow / accepted as an exception.
clarifications.answer: No. There are no Workflow Rule field updates or Process Builder processes on Opportunity, and the one record-triggered Flow we have only writes NextStep. Nothing writes Amount after save.

clarifications.question: Which users, profiles, or integrations must still be able to save a Closed Won Opportunity that would otherwise violate this rule (e.g. data loads, an ERP/CPQ sync, a manager issuing a credit memo, admins correcting an error) — and who is the accountable owner when the rule blocks a save that should have gone through?
clarifications.why: Every rule with no bypass blocks every data load and API write that doesn't meet the condition (admin/validation-rules, row 3); a rule with no named exception owner hides the trigger, the condition and the exception path from whoever hits it later (admin/requirements-gathering-for-sf, row 7).
clarifications.answer_shape: Given a save that would violate the rule, When it is attempted by [named profile / integration user / admin], Then it [is exempted via Custom Permission '<name>' carried by Permission Set '<name>' / is blocked, and <named role> is who the user contacts to fix it].
clarifications.answer: Only the Sales Ops team (two people) may correct a Closed Won Amount, and only via a documented bypass: grant them a custom permission checked by the rule (a permission set assigned to them), not a profile exemption. No integration user writes Amount.

clarifications.question: What should the validation error say, in 255 characters or fewer, naming both the problem and the fix?
clarifications.why: errorMessage is capped at 255 characters; a rule that can't say what to do generates a support ticket per occurrence (admin/validation-rules, row 5, and the skill's Error Message Standard: what went wrong / why / how to fix).
clarifications.proposed_default: "Amount cannot be decreased once this Opportunity is Closed Won. Amount is locked after close to protect the recorded deal value. Contact your manager to reopen the Opportunity before changing Amount."
clarifications.answer_shape: The final message text, not a placeholder — under 255 characters, stating the problem and the required next action.
clarifications.answer: Use the proposed default message as written.

clarifications.question: Does Opportunity data today already violate this rule — are there Closed Won Opportunities whose Amount has already been edited downward, or a legitimate recurring reason Amount decreases after close (refunds, credit memos, contract true-ups)?
clarifications.why: Validation rules fire on update as well as insert; an active rule on dirty data blocks every future edit of every violating record except the one that would fix it (admin/validation-rules, row 6).
clarifications.answer_shape: Given the Opportunity data as it exists today, When the rule is deployed, Then it deploys [active, because no known violations or legitimate decrease pattern exists] or [inactive with owner '<name>' and a target date for cleanup / for building the legitimate-decrease exception].
clarifications.answer: Yes, a handful of Closed Won Opportunities have had Amount lowered historically. Leave them as they are; no data clean-up is in scope. The rule only needs to stop it from now on.

clarifications.question: Roughly how many Opportunities move to Closed Won per day, and what is the largest single batch write to Opportunity anyone runs (data load, mass reassignment, a nightly sync)?
clarifications.why: A requirement's volume and its largest batch decide whether an unbypassed rule turns a routine load into a failed job the moment it touches one non-conforming record (admin/requirements-gathering-for-sf, row 3).
clarifications.answer_shape: A steady-state count per day and a worst-case batch size, so the rollout risk of Q3's bypass decision can be sized.
clarifications.answer: About 30 Opportunities move to Closed Won per day. The largest batch write is a quarterly Data Loader update of roughly 5,000 Opportunities that changes StageName and CloseDate but never Amount.

clarifications.question: Does Amount on a Closed Won Opportunity ever get written from outside Salesforce — an ERP, a CPQ tool, a billing system, or any inbound integration?
clarifications.why: A requirement sourced from or touched by an external system is an integration requirement wearing a validation-rule costume, and needs a pattern decision (bypass, or a contract change on the sending system) before this ships as a simple validation rule (admin/requirements-gathering-for-sf, row 4).
clarifications.answer_shape: Given the systems that can write Opportunity.Amount, When one of them is external, Then it is named, its integration user is covered by Q3's bypass decision, and — if the volume or coupling is more than one integration user needing a bypass — this build is re-scoped from 'ask' to 'feature'.
clarifications.answer: No. No ERP, CPQ or billing system writes Opportunity Amount; the only writers are Sales Cloud users in the UI and the quarterly Data Loader run in Q6, which does not touch Amount.

clarifications.question: Is Amount visible on every Opportunity page layout and for every record type this rule applies to?
clarifications.why: errorDisplayField silently changes to Top of Page when the field isn't visible on the layout in scope (admin/validation-rules, row 4).
clarifications.proposed_default: Amount is on the standard Opportunity layout(s) in scope; attach the error to the Amount field.
clarifications.answer_shape: Confirmation that Amount is on the layout(s) in scope, or the error message rewritten to read correctly at the top of the page.

clarifications.question: Does the rule's formula need to reference a compound field (Address, a person's Name) or a dependent picklist anywhere?
clarifications.why: Validation rules can't use compound fields as of API version 20.0 (admin/validation-rules, row 7).
clarifications.proposed_default: No — the rule references only Amount (Currency) and StageName (Picklist), neither of which is a compound field.
clarifications.answer_shape: Confirmation the formula touches only simple fields, or a rewrite against the component fields before anyone starts typing.

clarifications.question: Is there a workaround the team uses today to catch an Amount decrease after Closed Won (a report someone checks, a manual review), or is this a gap with no current safeguard?
clarifications.why: Stakeholders often describe the workaround they built around a missing control as if it were the requirement, and an As-Is step tagged keep/drop/replace stops the new rule from re-implementing a manual process nobody asked to keep (admin/requirements-gathering-for-sf, row 1).
clarifications.proposed_default: No current safeguard; the requirement itself states Amount 'can't go down' today, implying no control currently prevents it.
clarifications.answer_shape: Either 'no current workaround, this is net-new' or the workaround named and tagged drop (replaced by the rule) / keep (runs alongside it).

clarifications.question: Does this change require any new record-access or field-level-security restriction, or does the existing Opportunity sharing/FLS model apply unchanged?
clarifications.why: Record access and field access are different mechanisms configured in different places, and a validation rule changes neither by itself — an unstated visibility change would be silently missed (admin/requirements-gathering-for-sf, row 2).
clarifications.proposed_default: No new record-access or FLS change requested; the existing Opportunity sharing and field-level-security model applies unchanged.
clarifications.answer_shape: Confirmation of no sharing/FLS change, or a sharing_impact value naming the layer (OWD, role hierarchy, sharing rule, team, manual/Apex, restriction).

clarifications.question: Who exactly edits Opportunity Amount — an internal employee, or does a customer, partner, or contractor with portal access ever touch it?
clarifications.why: The answer selects a licence, and licence selects API allocation, object access and portal template long before design starts (admin/requirements-gathering-for-sf, row 5).
clarifications.proposed_default: Internal Sales Cloud users (employees) only, consistent with the requester (Sales Ops) and no portal/partner access implied by the requirement.
clarifications.answer_shape: Confirmation of internal-only access, or a licence_implication value naming the external persona and an escalation to architect/license-optimization-strategy.

clarifications.question: Does this requirement need a new report or dashboard number alongside the rule (e.g. a count of blocked saves), or is the rule a save-time control only?
clarifications.why: Reporting requirements assume joins the report-type rules forbid, and an unstated reporting need gets silently dropped between discovery and build if it isn't asked now (admin/requirements-gathering-for-sf, row 6).
clarifications.proposed_default: No new report requested; this is a save-time control only, not a reporting change.
clarifications.answer_shape: Confirmation no report is needed, or a reporting row naming base object, join chain, and whether rows must appear with no related record.

assumptions.text: Amount is visible on the standard Opportunity page layout(s) in the rule's scope, so errorDisplayField=Amount renders next to the field rather than relocating to Top of Page.
The rule's formula references only Amount (Currency) and StageName (Picklist) — no compound fields (address, person name, dependent picklist), which validation rules cannot use as of API 20.0.
No current workaround (report or manual review) catches an Amount decrease after Closed Won today; this rule is a net-new control, not a replacement for an existing safeguard.
No new record-access or field-level-security restriction is in scope; the existing Opportunity sharing and FLS model applies unchanged.
Only internal Sales Cloud (employee) users edit Opportunity Amount; no customer, partner, or contractor portal persona touches this field.
No new report or dashboard is requested alongside the rule; this is a save-time control only.

in: Block any Opportunity save that lowers Amount once StageName = Closed Won; Amount is typed directly on the Opportunity, no Opportunity Products / Line Items roll up into it (Q1).
Sales-Ops-only correction path via a named Custom Permission carried by a dedicated Permission Set, not a Profile exemption (Q3).

Deploy the rule active=true using a delta check (Amount < PRIORVALUE(Amount)) so it fires only on a further decrease and does not retroactively re-block the handful of historical violations, which are left as-is (Q5).
Error message fixed to the Q4 default text, attached to the Amount field, which is on the standard layout(s) in scope (Q4, Q8 default).
out: Cleaning up the historical Closed Won Opportunities whose Amount was already lowered — Q5 explicitly declines any data clean-up; carried as assumption via the delta-check design instead.
A record-triggered flow or Apex path for Amount — Amount is edited directly and no Opportunity Product / Line Item rollup exists (Q1), so the platform-native validation rule is sufficient.
Any bypass or contract change for an external system — no ERP, CPQ or billing system writes Amount; only Sales Cloud UI users and the Q6 quarterly Data Loader job, which does not touch Amount (Q7).
Any change to the Opportunity sharing or field-level-security model — the existing model applies unchanged (Q11 default, assumption A4).
A new report or dashboard counting blocked saves — save-time control only (Q13 default, assumption A6).

fit_gap.requirement: Lock Opportunity.Amount against a decrease once Closed Won, with a Sales-Ops-only bypass
fit_gap.note: Native ValidationRule with a PRIORVALUE delta check enforces the invariant; the bypass is a native CustomPermission read via $Permission and granted through a PermissionSet. No Apex, no Flow, no callout. Mechanism and bypass-pattern ranking (Custom Permission preferred over Profile/RecordType) per admin/validation-rules (Bypass patterns table, Formula Best Practices) and admin/custom-permissions (Pattern: Admin-Only Bypass in Validation Rules).

decisions.decision: Grant the Sales Ops bypass as a Custom Permission (Bypass_Opp_Amount_Lock) carried by a dedicated Permission Set (Opp_Amount_Lock_Bypass), rather than a Profile exemption or a RecordType-scoped exclusion.
decisions.rationale: standards/decision-trees/automation-selection.md and standards/decision-trees/sharing-selection.md were both checked against README.md's routing table; neither tree routes a validation-rule bypass mechanism (that is a bypass-pattern choice, not an automation or sharing-layer choice). admin/validation-rules' Bypass Patterns table ranks Custom Permission first ('Preferred — granular, auditable') ahead of RecordType scope and marks Profile check 'not recommended'; admin/custom-permissions' Pattern: Admin-Only Bypass in Validation Rules gives the identical two-artefact shape. Q3's answer independently rules out a profile exemption by name, so the requester's instruction and the skill's documented default agree.
decisions.consequences: The bypass is auditable via a SetupEntityAccess query and revocable per user without touching a profile, at the cost of two artefacts (CustomPermission + PermissionSet) instead of one; the validation-rule checker's VR-REF-02 $Permission resolution depends on the CustomPermission file being present in the same scan tree as the rule.

decisions.decision: Deploy the validation rule active=true despite existing historical Closed Won Opportunities whose Amount was already lowered, relying on a delta check (Amount < PRIORVALUE(Amount)) rather than an absolute check, so already-violating records are not retroactively re-blocked on unrelated edits.
decisions.rationale: No decision tree covers 'deploy a validation rule active vs inactive against known-dirty data.' The skill's own Questions-to-Ask row 6 and the PRIORVALUE gotcha establish that a delta-based formula fires only on a further decrease, so a record that is already a historical violation (a fact already true today) does not retrigger the rule on a save that leaves Amount unchanged or raises it; Q5's answer explicitly declines any data clean-up, which an active=false deploy would otherwise force.
alternatives_rejected: Deploy active=false pending a data-cleanup project
An absolute check disallowing any Amount below its value at the moment of Closed Won, regardless of edit direction
decisions.consequences: The handful of already-violating records remain permanently non-conforming by design; any future edit to Amount on those records that decreases it further is still blocked exactly like any other Closed Won record.

milestones.title: Lock Opportunity Amount after Closed Won
milestones.goal: Given a Closed Won Opportunity, when a user without the Bypass_Opp_Amount_Lock custom permission attempts to save a lower Amount, then the save is blocked with the Q4 error message; when a Sales Ops user holding the Opp_Amount_Lock_Bypass permission set makes the same edit, then the save succeeds.

acceptance_tests.description: Given a Closed Won Opportunity, when a user without the Bypass_Opp_Amount_Lock permission lowers Amount and saves, then the save is blocked and the error reads 'Amount cannot be decreased once this Opportunity is Closed Won. Amount is locked after close to protect the recorded deal value. Contact your manager to reopen the Opportunity before changing Amount.'; when a Sales Ops user holding the Opp_Amount_Lock_Bypass permission set makes the identical edit, then the save succeeds.
acceptance_tests.expected: ticked at the M1 milestone gate

steps.title: Amount_Locked_After_Closed_Won validation rule, with a Sales Ops bypass

inputs.errorConditionFormula:
AND(
  NOT($Permission.Bypass_Opp_Amount_Lock),
  NOT(ISNEW()),
  NOT(ISBLANK(TEXT(StageName))),
  ISPICKVAL(StageName, "Closed Won"),
  Amount < PRIORVALUE(Amount)
)

inputs.bypass_holders: Sales Ops team, 2 named users; no integration user (Q3, Q7)

verification.notes: scale: ask -- one verification round, refutation-only, over one step. No CRITICAL refutation as standards/build-orchestration.md Section 3.1 defines it at this tier (no ineligible agent, no unresolvable skill or template, no missing checker, no decision lacking a tree branch where one applies), so the outcome is verified with 10 warnings for the human to weigh at the single go gate. Two of the ten are notable and neither is fixable at this stage: W1 (access grant with human_gate: false, forced by Section 3.1 itself) and W2 (a milestone manual test that only a deployed org can settle). amend-step, which Section 3.1 names as the in-place remedy for a testability refutation, is refused by the CLI while the build status is planned or verified and cannot reach a milestone's acceptance tests at all.
